In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nitrile oxide is not the reactive species in the reaction.
the nitrile oxide is not an electrophile, but a nucleophile, and the reaction is a nucleophilic attack by the nitrile oxygen of a nitrile oxide on the carbon of a double bond.
the nitrone cycloaddition of 1,3-dipolarophiles to 5-methylene-hydantoins is regioselective and that the regiochemistry is determined by the electronic nature of the dipolarophile.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
atropisomerism in the nitrile oxide can be used to induce facial selectivity in cycloadditions of nitrile oxides with electron-deficient alkenes.
the cycloaddition of nitrile oxides with 5-methylenhydantoins is regioselective, and the facial selectivity can be controlled by atropisomerism of the 5-methylehydantoin moiety.
the cycloaddition of nitrile oxide and 5-methylene hydantoins is highly regioselective, and atropisomers of N-aryl 5-methylene-2-phenylhydantoins show a high degree of facial selectivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cycloadditions of 5-methylene-hydantoins with benzonitriles oxide are highly regioselective and atropisomerism in N-arylhydantoins can lead to facial selectivity.
the atropisomerism induced facial selectivity is an effective strategy to obtain 5-spirocycloadducts with complete facial selectivity.
the facial selectivity of these nitrile oxides is not only determined by the substituents on the nitrile oxide, but also by the substituants on the 5-methylene hydantoins.
